purpose: Source inventory of every allowlisted scheduler module and event handler; this is not an authorization or RLS policy.

shared_boundary.database_identity: Kernel worker and spawned children inherit the configured runtime PG_USER and PG_PASSWORD.
shared_boundary.signed_tenant_context: Not established by scheduler dispatch or generic event-handler spawn.
shared_boundary.module_argument_validation: Static module-specific operation schemas validate command_args before schedule activation, run-now, generated job plans, scheduler-allowlisted code-owned job runs, and worker subprocess creation. Unsupported manual/destructive operations and source-less recurring sensor ingestion fail closed; existing task rows are not rewritten.
shared_boundary.deployment_effect: Inventory only; it does not change grants, activate schedules, or enable RLS.

scheduled_modules.scope: Optional --location-id limits one location; omission scans all active locations with coordinates.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: weather_observation insert has no explicit conflict clause; ClickHouse projection is keyed by payload hash. A replay may create a second PostgreSQL observation.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: Scheduler retry can repeat provider reads and PostgreSQL inserts; no source watermark is recorded by this entrypoint.

scheduled_modules.scope: Global crop/commodity market data; optional commodity and period arguments filter the run.
external_effects: World Bank Pink Sheet HTTP download; optional built-in seed dataset
scheduled_modules.idempotency: price_observation uses ON CONFLICT (source, commodity_code, market_name, price_date) DO NOTHING.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: The natural key suppresses duplicate period rows; provider freshness and historical correction behavior are separate review questions.

scheduled_modules.scope: All active tracked wallets on configured chains unless --chain selects one chain.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: attestation_record uses attestation_uid conflict suppression; ClickHouse projection has an attestation UID key. The cursor stores a maximum attestation timestamp per chain.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: A retry repeats wallet/provider reads; late-arriving events at or below the stored timestamp require separate reconciliation.

scheduled_modules.scope: All active tracked wallets unless chain or wallet address selects a narrower source.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: wallet_activity_event suppresses duplicate transaction hashes; projection rows are queued by the stable source key.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: A retry repeats RPC reads. Reorg depth, checkpoint advancement, and completeness are not proven by the module allowlist.

scheduled_modules.scope: Rows inherit sensor location and plot; CLI modes accept a file or an identified sensor. The historical scheduled seed supplies no arguments and does not define an input source.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: sensor_reading is unique by sensor_id/date/time; duplicate timestamp values are compared and conflicting values fail. Event and projection writes share the ingestion transaction where enabled.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: A replay of the same row is deduplicated; the scheduled no-argument seed does not establish a valid recurring input contract.

scheduled_modules.scope: Configured Gnosis DAO/contracts and indexed protocol events; wallet ownership can resolve farm location rows.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: digital_lego_usage uses conflict suppression; governance_event and treasury_event inserts shown in the indexer do not declare a conflict clause. End-to-end replay idempotency is therefore not established.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: The indexer is global and checkpointed, but reorg/duplicate behavior must be verified per event table before automatic replay.

scheduled_modules.scope: The scheduled check can scan all active rules/readings or accept a sensor filter; the event handler is source-reading scoped.
external_effects: Scheduled CLI mode can send email and Directus notifications; event mode queues notifications durably. Actuation is recorded for later approval/execution in PostgreSQL; this module does not publish MQTT commands.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: The event handler reserves a per-source-reading/rule effect receipt and commits alert/claim/notification intent atomically. Actuation remains behind approval policy.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: A same-reading/rule retry is deduplicated; broader scheduled batch and external-provider recovery remain at-least-once.

scheduled_modules.scope: Metric compute supports one location or an --all-locations fanout; the separately contracted NOI snapshot reconciliation is global.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: Each compute inserts a new metric_value with verified=false; repeated calculations are not deduplicated by the engine. NOI snapshot reconciliation upserts by crop_cycle_id. Recalculation remains a draft write, never human verification.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: A scheduler retry may create another metric draft for the same location/period; snapshot reconciliation updates its natural-key row. Human review state remains separate.

scheduled_modules.scope: --check scans configured sources and all locations unless --source narrows the configuration set.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: Alert state is locked per source/location and transitions use cooldown logic; every check and provider attempt is retained. End-to-end provider delivery is at-least-once.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: Database state is durable; external delivery needs receiver idempotency or operator reconciliation.

scheduled_modules.scope: All active dashboard_dataset definitions selected by the CLI; result source is limited to the three curated reporting views when the feature is explicitly enabled.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: Refresh writes only a row count and metadata. The current SQL text and active state are compared at update time to reject stale results.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: KOKONUT_FEATURE_LEGACY_DATASET_SQL defaults off; enabled reads use the separate ACL-verified read-only analytics role.

scheduled_modules.scope: Exactly one required --location-id per process; --all means all climate providers for that location, not all locations.
external_effects: ERA5 Land (--ncep), MODIS, SMAP, and Sentinel-1 requests through Google Earth Engine; the worldclim command makes no network request and records a latitude_proxy_v1 estimate
scheduled_modules.idempotency: worldclim_climate uses a partial unique key for one location-level row (plot_id IS NULL); migration 397 refuses duplicate legacy rows without deleting them. GEE summary tables have no matching unique key and provider retries may insert duplicates.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: Per-location retry is the intended unit; GEE writes commit before ingestion_log writes, so a crash can leave an unlogged provider row. The historical seed's --all argument is invalid because --location-id is required.

scheduled_modules.scope: --process claims the global event queue; --notification-process claims the global notification outbox. Event handlers may be tenant-scoped, global, or external as recorded below.
external_effects: Delegated to registered event handlers; --notification-process may deliver email, webhook, or Directus notifications
scheduled_modules.idempotency: Per-event/per-handler receipts suppress already-successful handlers. Outbox enqueue uses stable source/channel/destination keys. Event and provider delivery remain at-least-once across lease expiry or a crash after an external effect.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: Event and notification queues use durable leases and bounded retries. Dead-letter replay/disposal and event cleanup are excluded from scheduled operation contracts; cleanup retention remains an owner decision.

scheduled_modules.scope: The only scheduled operation is --check-adjustments; it can scan all verified/published credits or filter to one --location-id.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: The check recomputes from current verified source rows and does not write credit adjustments, retirement state, or review decisions. Repeating it has no database side effects.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: Retry repeats bounded database reads and reports current differences. --adjust, issuance, retirement, and retirement-review flags are rejected by the scheduled command contract.

scheduled_modules.scope: Global projection queue; the supported scheduled operation is --run-once with a bounded batch (the current JobSpec fixes --limit 100). Operator list, replay, disposal, and manual reconciliation commands are excluded from scheduled arguments.
external_effects: When ClickHouse is enabled, writes allowlisted projection rows to the optional ClickHouse provider; when disabled, leaves queue rows untouched.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: Stable event keys and payload hashes suppress duplicate enqueue; lease tokens guard completion. External ClickHouse delivery is at-least-once across a crash after the provider write and before PostgreSQL completion.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: Expired claims are recovered and delivery retries are bounded at eight attempts before dead-lettering; every batch is capped at 1000 rows and the scheduled JobSpec requests 100.

event_handlers.scope: One event/source reading and its location; event execution still inherits the shared runtime database identity without signed tenant context.
event_handlers.idempotency: Per-reading/rule receipt; effects commit atomically before the parent worker stores its delivery receipt.
event_handlers.retry_boundary: The handler may run again after crash or lease expiry; its source-reading/rule effect receipt suppresses duplicate database effects, while notification delivery remains at-least-once.

event_handlers.scope: Global freshness alert identity; notification payload may contain location-scoped details.
event_handlers.idempotency: Stable source-event/channel/destination outbox key; remote delivery remains at-least-once unless the receiver honors the idempotency key.
event_handlers.retry_boundary: Event retry repeats durable enqueue, which conflicts on the stable event/channel/destination identity; provider sending and operator replay happen in the separate outbox worker.

event_handlers.scope: Requires and canonicalizes one payload location UUID before invalidating analytics cache entries; does not establish database tenant context.
event_handlers.idempotency: Repeated invalidation of the same location is idempotent; concurrent and crash/retry evidence exists for this handler.
event_handlers.retry_boundary: Lease expiry or crash may invoke invalidation again; repeated location-scoped invalidation is safe and does not affect other locations.

event_handlers.scope: Requires and canonicalizes one payload location UUID before invalidating CRISP cache entries; does not establish database tenant context.
event_handlers.idempotency: Repeated invalidation of the same location is idempotent; concurrency, timeout, lease takeover and crash/retry evidence exists for this handler.
event_handlers.retry_boundary: Lease expiry or crash may invoke invalidation again; repeated location-scoped invalidation is safe and does not affect other locations.

event_handlers.scope: Global notification outbox identity; payload content may reference a location.
event_handlers.idempotency: Stable source-event/channel/destination outbox key; remote delivery remains at-least-once unless the receiver honors the idempotency key.
event_handlers.retry_boundary: Event retry repeats durable enqueue, which conflicts on the stable event/channel/destination identity; provider sending and operator replay happen in the separate outbox worker.

known_open_items: Trace the transitive service/calculator/provider call graph for every scheduled command, including dynamic SQL and file/network effects.

Reconcile existing enabled scheduled_task rows and external scheduler definitions against the new operation contracts; invalid persisted rows fail before subprocess creation but are not automatically rewritten.
Provision a separate worker database principal and non-forgeable context contract before worker SQL can be trusted under RLS.
Do not enable application RLS or narrow broad runtime DML grants until the complete call graph, external/operator schedules, and owner mappings are reconciled.
